newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk to issue shares or bonds to cut debt.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk to issue shares or bonds to cut debt.

text.p: Russia's Norilsk Nickel 0#NKEL.RUO said its flagship metal producing combine would issue shares or bonds to help the group reduce its debts, the company said in a statement on Wednesday.

RAO Norilsky Nikel said last month that it owed workers at the flagship plant around 900 billion roubles and around 1.2 trillion roubles to various budgets. The statement gave no further details of the issue.
The company could not say which of the schemes proposed by the government early last month to help resolve its debt crisis would be adopted.
One plan envisaged the combine issuing shares. In this instance the company would pay off its main debt over a period of five years and fines on that debt over a period of 10 years.
A second plan envisaged the combine issuing bonds. In this case the company's main debt would be restructured over two years, and fines on the main debt over a period of five years.
A Norilsk official on Tuesday told Reuters in London that the group's management planned a share issue.
Russia's Uneximbank controls 51 percent of voting shares in the financially-troubled Norilsk Nickel group.
